title: Google DeepMind Ships Three Physical AI Models For Whole Body Control, Dexterity And Multi Robot Collaboration
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Google DeepMind has released Gemini Robotics 2, the intelligence layer for its next generation of robots. The release ships three models: a vision-language-action model for whole b...
body:
Google DeepMind has unveiled Gemini Robotics 2, a significant intelligence layer for next-generation robots. This release dramatically expands robotic capabilities beyond simple tabletop tasks, introducing comprehensive whole-body control, intricate five-finger dexterity, and advanced multi-robot collaboration. Delivered as three distinct models, Gemini Robotics 2 aims to overcome current limitations in robotic adaptability and skill transfer within dynamic, unpredictable environments.

The system operates through a specialized, modular design crucial for developers. **Gemini Robotics 2** acts as the core Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model, translating multimodal inputs into precise motor commands for full humanoids and bi-arm robots, enabling dexterous manipulation. For high-level strategic planning, the **Gemini Robotics ER 2** (Embodied Reasoning) model serves as the robot's brain, understanding human instructions and the physical world to plan complex, multi-step tasks. Built on Gemini 3.5 Flash, it processes extensive multimodal data. Complementing these, **Gemini Robotics On-Device 2** provides an optimized VLA for efficient local execution. This division allows ER 2 to orchestrate missions, delegating execution to VLA models registered as callable tools, offering flexible system design.

This innovative architecture empowers robots to move beyond rigid programming into adaptive, full-body control and complex reasoning. For researchers, it paves the way for truly autonomous and versatile robotic applications, unlocking new possibilities in human-robot interaction and real-world task execution. Gemini Robotics 2 represents a pivotal step towards more capable and responsive robotic systems.

title: Okta buys AI security startup Permiso; source says for about $200M
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: The deal gives Okta identity threat detection capabilities as enterprises seek to secure AI agents and other non-human identities across cloud environments.
body:
Okta has announced its agreement to acquire Permiso Security, an AI identity security startup, in a deal reportedly valued at just under $200 million. This strategic move underscores Okta's commitment to expanding its identity management capabilities beyond traditional user authentication to address the rapidly growing need for securing AI agents and other machine identities. As enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous software, the demand for continuous monitoring of what these non-human entities do post-access becomes paramount, intensifying competition in the identity security landscape.

Permiso's technology is designed to detect suspicious activities within cloud environments *after* initial access has been granted to users or applications. The startup excels at identifying attacks that leverage stolen or compromised identities to navigate cloud infrastructure. Crucially, Permiso has evolved its platform to specifically monitor AI agents and machine identities. Its innovative SandyClaw platform further enhances this by analyzing AI agent skills in a sandboxed environment, allowing for the identification of potentially malicious behaviors before these agents are deployed into live operations.

This acquisition is highly significant for developers and researchers, highlighting the critical shift in identity security towards protecting non-human entities in an AI-first world. It emphasizes that robust security frameworks must now encompass continuous threat detection and response for autonomous software, not just human users. For those building and deploying AI, it signals the necessity of integrating advanced identity threat detection and prevention capabilities from the ground up, ensuring the integrity and trustworthiness of AI systems as they become more deeply embedded across enterprise operations.

title: Advancing the price-performance frontier with GPT-5.6
author: Modelverse Editorial
excerpt: Explore lower GPT‑5.6 pricing for Luna and Terra—and how OpenAI’s more efficient models help enterprises deploy AI workflows at scale.
body:
OpenAI is making its advanced AI capabilities more accessible by announcing a significant reduction in pricing for its GPT-5.6 models, specifically for the Luna and Terra versions. This strategic move aims to lower the financial barrier for organizations looking to leverage state-of-the-art language models, making sophisticated AI more attainable for a broader spectrum of applications and users.

This enhanced affordability is a direct result of OpenAI's relentless pursuit of efficiency improvements within its model architectures and operational pipelines. Through continuous innovation in training methodologies and inference optimization, the company has managed to extract more performance per computational resource. These advancements translate into a more cost-effective delivery of powerful AI, allowing the same high-quality output at a reduced operational expenditure.

For developers and researchers, this price-performance breakthrough is particularly impactful. It dramatically lowers the cost of experimentation and large-scale deployment, empowering enterprises to integrate advanced AI workflows into their operations without facing prohibitive expenses. This fosters greater innovation, accelerates the development of AI-powered products and services, and enables the community to build more ambitious projects, ultimately driving the widespread adoption and practical application of AI across diverse industries.
